steps.prompt: Yesterday your friend Jay said to you, “I am going to win the race.” Today you tell your mom about it. Write what you’d say, without using Jay’s exact words.

cards.title: Reported speech
cards.body: Reported (indirect) speech tells what someone said without their exact words, so there are no quotation marks. It often uses “that”, which you can leave out: Jay said (that) he was going to win.

cards.title: Pronouns change
cards.text:
Jay: “I love my new bike.”
Reported: Jay said that he loved his new bike.
You to Jay: “You can borrow my helmet.”
Reported: I told Jay that he could borrow my helmet.
cards.note: Pronouns change to fit who is reporting: I → he or she, my → his or her, we → they, you → I, he, she or they.

cards.title: Backshift: one step back
cards.text:
am / is → was · are → were
will → would · can → could
has / have → had · eats → ate
ate → had eaten · may → might
cards.note: After a past reporting verb (said, told), the verb usually moves one step back in time, because the words were spoken in the past.

cards.title: When it’s still true
cards.telling: Ms. Lee said that the Earth went around the Sun.
cards.showing: Ms. Lee said that the Earth goes around the Sun.
cards.note: If something is still true now (a fact, or a plan that hasn’t happened yet), you can keep the present. When you’re not sure, shift it back.

prompts: Which change is easiest to forget: the pronoun or the verb? Show it with one of your sentences.
When might a writer choose reported speech instead of a direct quote?
